text:
ava: Noticed a new regression on prod-canary: opening a dashboard with large heatmaps causes a long stall when interacting with legends. Repro: open multi-heatmap dashboard (~150 series), hover legend, scrub timeline. Observed on Chrome/Linux and Safari.

liam: timeline? this after the prefetch TTL change and the new chunk-splitting patch?

ava: yep. Rollout at 03:18 UTC. We switched to finer-grained chunk-splitting + updated prefetch affinity.

rachael: can you share a short perf trace?

ava: quick flame: Main -> parse (35ms) -> layout (110ms) -> paint (260ms). Legend hover triggers scheduleRender -> heavy paint.

liam: 260ms paint on hover implies a chunk boundary landed in the hot path. Are legend utils in a separate async chunk now?

ava: exactly. legend-color-scale and legend-renderer moved into legend-chunk. On hover we hit a dynamic import and also get a kvcache miss which stalls the render. Warm loads look fine.

devops: infra-bot shows a spike in kvcache-miss rate coincident with the deploy across eu-west and us-east clusters. Routing policy deprioritised some canaries due to new weights.

rachael: quick mitigation: add a small shim to require legend-utils from heatmap entry so the chunk is fetched up-front. Could be a minimal rollback.

ava: tried a local shim: `import './legend-utils';` at the top of heatmap entry. Local canary: hover 95p reduced from ~260ms to ~28ms.

devops: deploy-bot: Deployed canary build 1764023467 (tags: legend-preload-shim).

liam: longer term we should mark interactive primitives as critical chunks or update the prefetcher to prioritize elements with an `data-interactive` annotation. Also consider bundling very small utils with primary consumer.

rachael: agree. Also add telemetry events: legend-hover-start / legend-render-end so we can tie UX latency to chunk fetch and kvcache miss traces.

infra-bot: noted. I will emit a canary alert rule if 95th percentile legend-hover latency increases by >50ms for a rollout window.

ava: filed follow-up PR to move legend-utils into heatmap entry and to mark it as critical in the webpack config. Also added tests to fail canary if async splits affect interaction latency.

liam: small note: routing affinity change also exposed that eu canaries were getting lower prefetch priority. We should validate routing weights during rollout validation.

rachael: thanks team. Hotfix works in canary; rolling to 10% while we ship the permanent fix. :thumbsup:
